narratives.Overview:
## Summary

evaluateCompletedArcRecord never consults isInFlightCritiqueThread on a later arc, so a thread mid-critique stays ingestable

## Context

Issue bxc-3ci/FreshserviceAI#625 ran two design-critique arcs. Throughout both, deft issue:ingest would harvest the standing lean's items as the next-build contract while three critics were mid-flight arguing that two of those items could not be built as written.

## Expected behavior

While a critique arc is in flight on an issue, ingest is blocked or warned, so no worker harvests a contract the panel is actively refuting.

## Actual behavior / gap

In @deftai/directive-core 0.117.0 dist/design-critique/completed-arc-record.js, evaluateCompletedArcRecord consults isInFlightCritiqueThread only on the branch reached when no synthesis-accepted-shaped comment exists. Once a complete record exists and cites the latest lean, the function returns complete and the in-flight signal is never read. Every later arc opens on a thread that already carries a completed record, so the in-flight branch is unreachable for later arcs by construction.

## Session notes

Reproduced on a synthetic thread shaped like this one: lean with an empty path token plus digest, claims table, synthesis citing both, later-arc triage carrying mechanism-shaped true, then a panel deposit naming round 1 and siblings 3. Verdict is complete in all three variants while isInFlightCritiqueThread on the same comment set returns true. The incidental guards do not fire either: hashIssueBodyBytes over the live REST body equals the lean digest, so the stale-target path does not block. Workaround used: deft scm issue work-claim applies status:claimed, which session-start and xbrief:preflight scan, but it does not block ingest.

### Comment by @MScottAdams (2026-09-15T23:44:31Z)

model: grok-4.6
role: critic

Refutation charter against: a complete completed-arc record citing the latest successor lean makes ingest safe even when a later arc is in flight.

Verdict: that presumption is false. Round 1, N=1, ceiling 5689610808. Pin SHA f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352. I did not read comments after that id.

## 1. Later-arc in-flight still returns complete — blocks-the-design

Evidence. I ran `evaluateCompletedArcRecord` and `assertCompletedArcAllowsIngest` from `git show f2590baf5492c2e463d406883469433fe75b4352:packages/core/src/design-critique/completed-arc-record.ts` (workspace HEAD is that SHA; no dist). Bound fixture: Stop 1 with pain P1, standing map with Spec-path harvest list and matching body digest, critic targeting pain-P1, table, synthesis-accepted shape citing that map. Then later-arc add-ons, no new successor-lean heading:

- later `mechanism-shaped: true` only → status complete; ingest ALLOWS
- that plus panel-deposit `siblings: 3` → complete; ALLOWS
- that plus a later `role: critic` finding → complete; ALLOWS
- later Stop 1 with the same pain P1 already relieved by the standing map, plus deposit plus critic → complete; ALLOWS
- `evaluateTargetDigestAdmission` on the standing map vs the live body → status match
- `isInFlightCritiqueThread` on the bound-only thread is already true

`git show` of that file: `isInFlightCritiqueThread` is defined once and called once, after the complete-records early return. Matching complete records return `finalizeComplete` (pain coverage + set-level refuse) and never reach that call. `assertCompletedArcAllowsIngest` throws only on `blocked`. `packages/core/src/intake/issue-ingest.ts` then, on status complete, harvests a Spec-path Bound-remedy list from the cited map.

Existing first-arc tests already block a panel-deposit or critic with no record. The later-arc critic round is before a new successor-lean heading, so the latest-lean mismatch path does not fire. That is the window the filing describes.

Failure mode. `issue:ingest` harvests the standing Bound-remedy items as the next-build contract while later-arc critics are mid-flight arguing those items cannot be built as written. Occupancy and `status:claimed` do not throw on that path.

Disposition. The named presumption cannot bind. Ingest clearance that stops at "complete record cites the latest successor lean" is not later-arc safe.

## 2. Calling isInFlightCritiqueThread on the whole thread is not the close — sharpens-framing

Evidence. The same run: `isInFlightCritiqueThread(bound-only)` is true because the predicate ORs successor-lean heading, `role: critic`, `mechanism-shaped: true`, and panel-deposit. A finished bound thread always carries a successor-lean heading. Consulting that function as written on `recutComments` after a matching complete record would refuse every bound ingest, not only a later arc.

Inventory, before a new scanner:

- Latest-lean mismatch (`missing-record`) already refuses a later successor-lean heading with no new record. Locked in `completed-arc-record.test.ts` ("blocks a recut lean with no new synthesis yet"). That is after the critic window.
- `applyPainCoverage` / `latestStop1` is a different conjunct. Same run: later Stop 1 with new pain P2 → `malformed-pain` because the standing map still cites P1; later Stop 1 with no pain list → `missing-pain`; later Stop 1 that reuses already-relieved P1 → still complete. Pain coverage is not later-arc in-flight.
- Catalog chips are not clearance. Labels are not predicates. Leftover `mechanism-shaped` does not block a complete record (existing test).
- `status:claimed` / work-claim warns at session-start and preflight; it does not throw in `assertCompletedArcAllowsIngest`.
- Stale-target is a body-hash pin. This run matched.

Existing predicate reuse that does not invent a scanner: call `isInFlightCritiqueThread` on comments with id greater than the matching complete record's synthesis id. On a rebound later arc, matching is the new record and that suffix is empty. On this hole, the suffix is critic / panel-deposit / `mechanism-shaped: true` while the latest successor-lean heading is still the bound one. `missing-record` is already published; do not add an unpublished reason code.

Failure mode. A drop-in consult either blocks all bound ingest or, if someone then special-cases successor-lean heading out, still misses that the hole is the suffix after complete, not "in-flight anywhere."

Disposition. The close can bind if it is "in-flight after the matching complete record," not "consult `isInFlightCritiqueThread` on the thread that already bound."

## 3. Pain-coverage incidental blocks and digest match — footnote

Later Stop 1 with a new pain id or a missing pain list does block, and a matching Target-digest does not. Those are real, and they are not the later-arc critic window. Do not treat them as coverage of P1.

## Injection / swarm

The target is ingest clearance over a shared issue thread. Spec-path harvest writes plan items from the standing map while later-arc critics on that same number are live. Work-claim and occupancy do not serialize that harvest. The standing map is the harvest source; the later-arc comments are not. Untrusted later-arc text is not the injection; the clearance hole is concurrent harvest of a contract the live panel is refuting.

## Road not taken

I considered using catalog chip `in-progress` as the gate. Chips are list state, leftover `mechanism-shaped` does not block, and chip apply miss is non-blocking. I considered requiring a successor-lean heading on the later-arc Stop 1 write-back. That recuts "successor lean after same-round siblings," which is protocol, not an evaluator slice over comments already on the thread.

## Steelman

Strongest defense of the target: latest-lean mismatch plus pain coverage already refuse later-arc ingest, so complete-citing-latest-lean is the right clearance. What would flip: one measured later-arc in-flight case (critic or panel-deposit, no new successor-lean heading) that already returns `blocked` for a published reason about in-flight. This run did not produce that. Pain-list mismatch is a different conjunct and does not fire when the standing map already relieves the later Stop 1 ids.

## 2. Suffix consult must run on a finalizeComplete complete result — sharpens-framing

Evidence. Same run: later Stop 1 with new pain P2 plus deposit plus critic is already `malformed-pain`; later Stop 1 with no pain list is already `missing-pain`. Disposition. The close can bind if the suffix consult runs only when `finalizeComplete` returned complete. Incidental pain and set-level refuses keep their published reasons. This is scope of bullets 1-2, not a second close.

## Steelman

Strongest defense of relieves: P1: suffix consult of the existing predicate refuses the filed add-ons (measured), whole-thread consult would refuse every finished ingest (bound-only `isInFlightCritiqueThread` is true because a finished thread carries a successor-lean heading), rebound after a new successor-lean heading plus a citing record stays complete (measured), and missing-record is already the first-arc in-flight reason so reusing it avoids an unpublished code. What would flip: one measured filed-window case (later critic, panel-deposit, or later-arc `mechanism-shaped: true`, latest successor-lean heading still bound, no new heading) that still returns complete under the suffix consult. This run did not produce that. What this run did produce is the published missing-record recovery restoring complete in that same window, and both published missing-record details being false of it.
